claims.claim: The concept of a carapace is not limited to hard armor and can include soft protective items such as masks, respirators, cooling garments, hazmat gear, and face shields.
claims.supporting_excerpt: examples of what I am calling “carapace” can perfectly well be soft, like the surgical masks and respirators that were already used in cities with high levels of particulate air pollution, became ubiquitous in many places during the pandemic, and are now being repurposed across North America as protection from hazardous levels of near-surface wild ﬁre smoke. Other examples might include everything from the cooling garments increasingly worn by military personnel and ﬁrst responders working in extreme conditions, to encapsulated hazmat gear, to the heat-resistant face shields used by welders and furnace operators.

claims.claim: Personal protective equipment may not be net beneficial even for individual users due to added weight and environmental footprints, but it will still be marketed and used by those who can access it.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Such personal protective equipment will not necessarily be net bene ﬁcial even for individual users, given its additional weight, and it can have signi ﬁcanthand microplastic footprints of its own; but that is unlikely to prevent it being marketed, bought, and used by people who can access it.

definitions.definition: Personal protective equipment and apparatuses, which can be soft or hard, used to protect individuals from environmental hazards such as pollution, smoke, extreme heat, and toxic conditions.
Apparatuses that facilitate sensation, perception, and possibly action or interaction at a distance from the body.

distinctions.distinction: Carapace functions as personal protective equipment worn on the body for shielding against hazardous external conditions, whereas prosthesis refers to apparatuses facilitating remote sensation, perception, action, or interaction at a distance.

parsed.segment_function: Elaborate on the concepts of carapace and prosthesis as types of artificial adaptation to environmental threats, explaining their various forms, functions, and limitations.
